can_answer_question: partly: this data has no miles-driven exposure, so it cannot measure deaths per mile or whether per-mile risk declined; it can show annual counts of motorist deaths in reported crashes as a non-rate trend.
metric: Annual number of motorist deaths reported in NYC motor vehicle crashes, summed from number_of_motorist_killed.
denominator: None; this is a count, not a rate.
population: Police-reported NYC motor vehicle crash records dated 2013 through 2025, inclusive; the metric sums the reported motorist deaths in those records.
years: 2013-2025 inclusive; check whether either endpoint year is only partially covered.

data_check.facts: The planned period contains 2,132,218 source crash rows. Each year 2013-2025 has observed dates from January 1 through December 31; no edge year is visibly partial by its observed date bounds. Within the planned population, crash_date is non-missing by the year filter, no checked sentinel date occurs, and number_of_motorist_killed is missing in 0 rows in every year.
data_check.decision: No change to the plan. Keep all crashes in the year range and sum the motorist-deaths field; there are no rows to drop or count differently for a missing outcome. The year endpoints are fully represented at the observed date bounds.

limitations: The crash file has no vehicle-miles-traveled or other mileage exposure, so this is an annual fatality count, not a per-mile risk or rate. Full-year observed date bounds do not establish that every record is complete or that no dates are missing within the year.
